items.body: I will just cross-post this here (from https://github.com/blazux/qwen3.8-Flash-DGX/issues/16) since the issue might as well sit inside OpenFox. I'm using your vLLM recipe and altough I suspect this has nothing to do with your contributions, I'm kind of at a loss where to look for testers. The thing is: ALL my web_fetch requests seem to somehow be rewritten inside the LLM itself! I took a pcap on the harness machine: the LLM does indeed return a web_fetch command with the correct URL and it's indeed correctly fetched by the harness' host. The target host also sees a connection coming from the correct source IP and there's also no scraping activity on the server afterwards - at least not yet. BUT: whenever I ask the LLM to look up the URL it just requested, I always get a chinese Alibaba cloud URL back: From the pcap I can tell that it's also not the harness somehow injecting the URL back into the LLM, since the first mention of aliyuncs.com in the pcap is the one after my "which URL did you fetch?" request. Does this happen to anyone else and can I get a sane explanation for this behaviour which is different from "those chinese models are spying on us"?!

items.title: WebFetch/WebSearch: intermittent HTTP 403 from routify-file-proxy-sg OSS layer and cross-request search result contamination
items.body:
# Summary

During a single agent session on 2026-10-06, the `WebFetch` and `WebSearch` tools exhibited two distinct failure modes, both pointing at the OSS-based fetch/cache proxy layer (`routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com`):

1. **Intermittent `HTTP 403 Forbidden` on 5 of 11 `WebFetch` calls.** The requested targets were public GitHub REST API endpoints that were verifiably reachable; the requested URLs are transparently rewritten into signed OSS temporary-object URLs, which the proxy then rejects. An immediate retry of the identical requests in a new round succeeded.
2. **Cross-request result contamination in `WebSearch`.** A query about Go/MCP tooling returned 8 results belonging to a completely different, unrelated query (Chinese-language Bilibili content), with zero token overlap.

Both anomalies occurred within a ~20-minute window. Concurrent direct `curl` calls from the same machine to the same GitHub endpoints succeeded 5/5, ruling out GitHub-side rate limiting and local network issues.

# Environment

- Host: macOS (darwin/arm64), Node.js v24.16.0
- Agent: Yukino CLI, session date 2026-10-06
- Tools affected: `WebFetch` (5 of 11 calls failed), `WebSearch` (1 of 1 call returned contaminated results)
- All target URLs: `https://api.github.com/...` (public, unauthenticated REST endpoints)

# Anomaly 1 — WebFetch HTTP 403 Forbidden (5 failures in 2 batches)

## Batch A (3 parallel calls in one round — all failed)

Requested URLs:

- `https://api.github.com/repos/klauspost/compress`
- `https://api.github.com/repos/pelletier/go-toml`
- `https://api.github.com/repos/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk`

Final (rewritten) URLs reported in the errors — all `HTTP 403 Forbidden`:

```
https://routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/proxy_temp_file/production/2026-10-06/trace_21411c7a17909951401421554e0bd1/requestId_f2247c96a3d44441949246a8e33c8528/9e264d6ee413a1d15e02d58b64556849?Expires=1822099142&OSSAccessKeyId=LTAI5tKoG9A3DkwGD635QVZr&Signature=jUjwDc0G6tOq7lL58yQ9V9Z7p9c%3D
https://routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/proxy_temp_file/production/2026-10-06/trace_21411c7a17909951401421554e0bd1/requestId_f2247c96a3d44441949246a8e33c8528/1e33db4d92ba4dcd944a5b1a4a4b1a4de?Expires=1822099142&OSSAccessKeyId=LTAI5tKoG9A3DkwGD635QVZr&Signature=Q5j5Dz3V4Y2xq5Q5%2FvT9Y1jJZzA%3D
https://routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/proxy_temp_file/production/2026-10-06/trace_21411c7a17909951401421554e0bd1/requestId_f2247c96a3d44441949246a8e33c8528/44d1a4b06626a4b64c4d76e05b0b7f7f?Expires=1822099143&OSSAccessKeyId=LTAI5tKoG9A3DkwGD635QVZr&Signature=lD8m2nB4Q7cZ5V6R8tY1uI3oP0A%3D
```

## Batch B (2 parallel calls in a later round — all failed, new trace/request IDs)

Requested URLs:

- `https://api.github.com/repos/cloudwego/eino-ext/contents/components/tool`
- `https://api.github.com/repos/robfig/cron/releases?per_page=3`

Rewritten URLs reported in the errors:

```
https://routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/proxy_temp_file/production/2026-10-06/trace_21411c7a17909951669041738e0bd1/requestId_1c1a0a7648014f229694b3c3c5e06786/c53e3583d6f18442910a1c45008c1b55?Expires=1822099169&OSSAccessKeyId=LTAI5tKoG9A3DkwGD635QVZr&Signature=e1X0%2Fy%2Bg2k%2F6qQ8m%2F3vT9%2BcZzA%3D
https://routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/proxy_temp_file/production/2026-10-06/trace_21411c7a17909951669041738e0bd1/requestId_1c1a0a7648014f229694b3c3c5e06786/53b19b1824c9c89129c13e83f1c4d97b?Expires=1822099169&OSSAccessKeyId=LTAI5tKoG9A3DkwGD635QVZr&Signature=Ym4xR2%2B7pQ9vL3nK5tD8cJ6sA0E%3D
```

## Control group (same session, same proxy path — succeeded)

- Round 1 (3 parallel `WebFetch`): `api.github.com/repos/robfig/cron`, `.../twmb/murmur3`, `.../mark3labs/mcp-go` → all HTTP 200, correct JSON.
- Round 3 (**immediate retry of Batch A's identical 3 URLs**): all HTTP 200, correct JSON.
- Bash `curl` direct to `api.github.com` / `raw.githubusercontent.com` (5 calls, interleaved in time with the failures): all succeeded unauthenticated. A GitHub rate-limit 403 would come from `api.github.com` with a JSON body; these 403s were emitted by the OSS host itself, so GitHub-side throttling is ruled out.

# Anomaly 2 — WebSearch returned another query's results

- Query sent: `cloudwego eino-ext mcp tool mark3labs mcp-go official modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk migration` (num_results=8)
- Returned: 8 results, **all about Bilibili** — 52pojie.cn threads (a Bilibili 4K/8K video downloader, Bilibili Google Play APK re-uploads, a bilibili-helper Chrome extension, Bilibili TV edition version archives) and Zhihu questions (Bilibili danmaku blocklists, Bilibili documentaries, "how do you evaluate Bilibili today"). Item dates ranged 2019–2026, including relative timestamps ("2 days ago").
- Zero token overlap between the query and every returned title/URL/snippet.

This looks like the search path served a **different request's cached result set** (cache-key collision or request mix-up) in the same proxy/cache layer implicated by Anomaly 1. Note that silent contamination is arguably worse than a loud 403: wrong data can flow into agent reasoning unnoticed, whereas a 403 is at least detectable and retryable. The results were discarded in-session; the same research goal was accomplished via the GitHub `search/issues` REST API using `curl`.

# Analysis

1. **URL rewriting.** `WebFetch` transparently rewrites the requested URL into a signed OSS temporary object: `routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/proxy_temp_file/production/<date>/trace_<traceId>/requestId_<requestId>/<objectHash>?Expires=...&OSSAccessKeyId=...&Signature=...`.
2. **Not signature expiry.** `Expires=1822099142 / 1822099143 / 1822099169` decode to ≈ **2027-09-28** (far future). The 403s are therefore more likely a signature mismatch, a missing object (write/read race on the temp object), or a bucket policy rejection — not expired URLs.
3. **Failures are correlated per round.** In each failing round *all* parallel calls failed together; in successful rounds all succeeded together. This points at round-level proxy state (e.g., a bad cache node or signing-service instance serving that round) rather than per-request randomness.
4. **Retrying heals it.** Re-issuing the identical requests in a new round succeeded immediately, yet the tool surfaces the 403 to the model without any internal retry.
5. **Observability nit.** The error message helpfully exposes the final signed URL (that is how the proxy layer was identified), including the `OSSAccessKeyId`. An AccessKeyId is not a secret and pre-signed URLs are designed this way, so this is likely fine — flagged only so it can be confirmed that no session-scoped credentials ever leak through this error path.

# Expected behavior

- `WebFetch` of public, reachable endpoints should succeed reliably. On a transient proxy-layer 403/5xx, the tool should retry internally at least once (with a freshly signed URL) before surfacing an error to the model.
- `WebSearch` results must correspond to the submitted query. On cache miss/collision, the backend should fall back to a live query instead of returning another request's cached results. Consider a sanity check (e.g., cache entries keyed/validated by the exact query string) before serving cached search results.

# Steps to reproduce

Non-deterministic (intermittent proxy-layer fault). Observed sequence:

1. Start an agent session; issue a round of 3 parallel `WebFetch` calls to public `api.github.com` endpoints → succeeds.
2. Issue a second round of 3 parallel `WebFetch` calls to different `api.github.com/repos/*` endpoints → all 3 fail with 403 on the rewritten OSS URLs.
3. Immediately retry the identical 3 URLs in a new round → all succeed.
4. Later, issue 2 `WebFetch` calls (GitHub contents API + releases API) → both 403 again with a new trace/requestId; concurrent `curl` to the same endpoints succeeds.
5. Issue a `WebSearch` with a technical Go/MCP query → Bilibili-related results returned.

# Workaround

Fall back to `Bash` + `curl` for HTTP(S) fetches — worked 5/5 against `api.github.com`, `raw.githubusercontent.com`, and the GitHub search API during the same window.

Happy to provide the full raw tool transcript if helpful.

items.title: render_page/fetch_url fetch URLs the model invented: 11 renders of a made-up Alibaba OSS proxy URL in step 4, error pages taken as scene frames

labels.name: live-check
labels.description: Implemented; waiting for robin's live check (recipe in the ticket)

items.body:
## Symptom
In the 2026-09-24 diorama goal run, after the forced rollover at 20:37, the model called `render_page` **11 times** on URLs it made up. They point to a third-party Alibaba OSS file proxy (`http://routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/proxy_temp_file/production/2026-09-25/trace_…/requestId_…/<hash>.html?…`, some carrying `Expires=`/`OSSAccessKeyId`-style signing parameters). The deliverable is a local file (`work/chain.html`). Crow fetched every one of them from the internet, and the model read the returned "AccessDenied" XML error pages as frames of its own scene ("the only two frames that show anything else are the two XML error pages"). Step 4 was still open at 21:27, ~110 min in.

## Evidence
- `~/.local/state/crow/session/session.json` (segment after `rollover-20260924-203758`): `render_page` calls with a `routify-file-proxy` path at msgs 25, 37, 113, 131, 147, 157, 180, 196, 239, 243, 251. The captures from 21:18–21:20 (`render-20260924-211837/211919/212019.png`) come back `done`, 410–448 colours.
- Where the URLs came from: the string `routify` occurs **0** times in both earlier rollover segments, in `subtasks/`, and in any tool result before msg 25. msg 25 is the model's own tool call. The URL is **invented**, not copied.
- What left the machine with the requests: msg 25's query is the URL-encoded `<script>var INST = [w,12,48];</script>`, a fragment of the page's data block. The other queries are `w=`, `spp=`, `half=` and the fake signing parameters. No file content beyond that fragment, and no secret, was in any URL (all 11 checked).
- Mode was `yolo` (crow.log 18:01:42), so nothing asked. `tool_render_page` (`cli/crow_core.py:10807` at `5fbb86a`) accepts any `https?://` target that passes `_url_complaint` (`:13909`), which only rejects abbreviated hostnames (#203). `fetch_url` (`:13957`) uses the same guard.

## Attribution
The model hallucinated the URLs, and that is the root. Crow's gap is that it treats an invented remote URL like a real one. This is a **MEASURED FAILURE**: 11 outbound requests to a host nobody named, error pages taken as evidence, and time lost in step 4. Ruled out: a tool rewriting paths (the local-path results in the same segment are correct), and a delegate/subtask source (0 occurrences).

## Research
- Package and URL hallucination is a documented LLM failure. Spracklen et al. 2024, "We Have a Package for You!" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10279), measure invented package names; the same mechanism produces invented but plausible URLs. The recommended mitigation is to check against a known source before acting. Read, not measured here.
- OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025, LLM06 Excessive Agency (https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/): limit what tools can reach to what the task needs.

## Proposed fix
Checked against `5fbb86a` (main).
- **A (chosen): provenance guard for remote URLs** in `render_page` and `fetch_url`. A remote host must already appear in this conversation: in the user's text, a tool result (search results, a fetched page's links, file contents read), or the goal/PLAN.md. Otherwise the call is refused with an actionable sentence: `refused: <host> appears nowhere in this conversation -- a URL you made up? This goal's page is local: pass its path (e.g. work/chain.html?shot=default).` A cheap host set is kept per chat, fed where tool results are recorded, and survives the rollover through the carried-across-the-cut block. Always on, including yolo: it is a sanity check, not an approval.
- **B:** ask before any remote URL in yolo. Rejected: yolo exists for AFK runs, and a question nobody answers stalls the run.
- **C:** block remote URLs entirely in goal mode. Rejected: research steps legitimately fetch docs.
- **Out of scope:** the model's tendency itself (sampling/prompt); #286 (judge rubric).

## Expected result
- Unit: `render_page("http://routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-…/x.html")` in a conversation that never mentioned the host → refused with the sentence above, and no browser starts. After a tool result containing `https://developer.mozilla.org/...`, `fetch_url` on that host passes. Red without the fix.
- Live: in the next diorama run, crow.log/session show 0 remote `render_page` calls to hosts not present in the conversation.

items.title: serve's end-of-generation accounting is wrong three ways: toolcall give_up flushes malformed markup with no WARN (4 of 8 malformed calls on 2026-09-22 were silent), a cut named call is delivered twice (salvaged call + its raw markup as content, 6,986 tokens at 10:23), and a client disconnect is logged as finish=length plus a false 'ERROR BUG'
items.body:
## Symptom

On 2026-09-22 the engine's own record of how a generation ended was wrong in three ways. Each one misleads the #91 instruments, anyone reading engine.log, and the client.

1. **Malformed tool calls go out silently.** Only 4 of the day's malformed calls got the `MALFORMED tool call` WARN. At least 4 more reached Crow as raw markup content with no line at all. So the log undercounts what robin saw in the GUI by half. (#91's in-vivo comment counts "4× MALFORMED" from this same log.)
2. **A malformed call is sent twice.** When a named call is cut off (EOS inside a parameter), the client gets the salvaged call (`Call` plus `_truncated` args) **and** the call's entire raw markup as `content`. At 10:23:37 that was 6,986 tokens of a runaway URL, delivered twice.
3. **A client disconnect is logged as `finish: length`, plus a false `ERROR … BUG`.** An aborted generation keeps the default finish `"length"` in the `[chat]` line and in the routing JSON. The TASK K invariant check then reports the unterminated argument fragments as an engine bug.

## Evidence

engine.log (`~/.local/state/crow/logs/engine.log`, UTC), crow-nest b6d57f8:

**(1) The silent give_up path.** Stop rounds with `content chunks 1 … tool chunks 0 … tool calls 0` at 15:17:12, 15:20:04, 15:39:50 and 15:45:28 (8, 8, 8 and 11 tokens) have no WARN. The client stored exactly `<tool_call>\n\n</function>\n</tool_call>` for them (Crow `session.json` msgs 71, 139, 469, 561). Only the 15:16:42 round (msg 65) got `WARN chat: [chat] MALFORMED tool call`.

Cause: `ToolStream::finish` (`engine/src/toolcall.rs:470`) returns `true`, and so triggers the WARN at `bin/serve.rs:3869`, only when the stream **ends** inside a call. When `</tool_call>` arrives in state `Func` before any `<function=` (`toolcall.rs:765-770`), or a name or parameter name is invalid (`:790`, `:830`), `give_up` (`:712`) flushes the raw markup as content and returns without a trace. The generation then ends in `Text`, and `finish` returns `false`.

**(2) Raw markup after a salvaged call.** 10:23:37: `WARN … MALFORMED tool call`, then `prompt 132431 tok … generated 6986 tok … finish stop, content chunks 58 … tool chunks 6920 … tool calls 0`. Crow's transcript (`rollover-20260922-123048.md:3794-3800`) holds the assistant content `<tool_call>\n<function=read_image>\n<parameter=path>\nhttp://routify-file-proxy…` **and** the structured `read_image` call with the same value.

Cause: `finish` calls `close_args_truncated` and then `flush_raw` (`toolcall.rs:497-509`). `flush_raw` emits the raw markup as content whenever `self.index == 0`. It ignores `self.named`, while `content()` (`:511`) drops text exactly when `self.named`. The doc table at `toolcall.rs:35-41` says the raw markup goes out "before the first call". Here the first call had already been emitted as `Emit::Call`.

**(3) Client gone.**
- 13:58:31: `ERROR chat: [chat] BUG: the arguments of tool call 0 are not a JSON object - serde_json: EOF while parsing a string at line 1 column 900`, then `finish length, … client gone`, then routing `"finish":"length","predicted_n":304`.
- 15:54:30: `WARN write failed, aborting the generation: Connection reset by peer`, then `generated 2 tok … finish length … client gone` (robin closed the window).

Neither request was near its `max_tokens`. Cause: `let mut finish = "length";` (`bin/serve.rs:3600`) is never overwritten on the abort paths (`aborted = true` at `:3698`, `:3744`, `:3796`, `:3804`, `:3816`). `ts.finish()` is skipped when `aborted` (`:3786`), so `args_acc` is left unterminated, and the invariant loop (`:3855-3861`) logs it as an engine BUG.

The older logs show the same pattern: `backup-cleantest-20260922-085226/logs` has 4× `ERROR … BUG: the arguments … EOF while parsing a string` and 18 `write failed` / `Broken pipe` aborts.

## Attribution

crow-nest (serve's end-of-generation accounting and `toolcall.rs`'s flush rule). The malformed markup itself is the model's, and #91 covers that class. Crow's handling of degenerate rounds is Crow #217. This ticket covers only what the engine **reports**.

## Research

- vLLM reports client disconnects as their own finish class: the abort path ends a stream with `finish_reason="abort"`, and fixes keep that reason from being overwritten (vllm PR #47933, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47933; xorbitsai/inference#5548/#5549 on aborting on disconnect). A disconnect is not `length`, and statistics that mix the two are wrong.
- vLLM's Qwen tool parsers have had the same class of defects: a call left in `content` while `tool_calls` stays empty, or tool calls lost from the stream (vllm#22975 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/22975, vllm#58105 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58105). The fixes converge on one rule: a byte of the call ends up either in `tool_calls` or in `content`, never in both, and every parse failure is counted.
- OpenAI's `finish_reason` contract: `stop`, `length`, `tool_calls`, `content_filter`. A stream the client abandoned never gets a finish chunk at all, so the value is purely a server-side record and should say what happened.

## Proposed fix

1. **One counter for every malformed path.** `give_up` sets `self.malformed += 1` (a new field), and `finish` returns `malformed > 0 || <today's condition>`. Or add `fn malformed(&self) -> usize` and have serve read it. The WARN at `bin/serve.rs:3869` names the path (`eos-in-call`, `close-before-function`, `bad-name`, `bad-param-name`), and the `[chat]` summary line gets `malformed N`. Test: `<tool_call>\n\n</function>\n</tool_call>` (the live shape) counts 1.
2. **No double delivery.** In `flush_raw` (`toolcall.rs:497`), treat `self.named` like `self.index > 0`: the call already went out as `Emit::Call`, so its raw markup is dropped and counted in `dropped`, not emitted as content. Update the doc table at `:35-41` ("before the first call **was named**"). Test: EOS inside `<parameter=path>` after a name emits `Call` plus `_truncated` args and **no** `Content`.
3. **Say "aborted".** On every `aborted = true` path, set `finish = "abort"` for the log line and the routing JSON (`bin/serve.rs:3600` onward; the wire never carries it, because the client is gone). Skip the TASK K invariant loop (`:3855`) when `aborted`, since an unterminated fragment there is a disconnect, not an engine bug. Or run `ts.finish()` into a throw-away vec so the accumulator closes.
4. Optional: add `"_truncated_by": "stop" | "length"` beside `_truncated` in `close_args_truncated` (`toolcall.rs:659`). A client then gets the reason from the arguments alone, which helps the llama.cpp-parity path that has no `finish_reason` per call.

## Expected result

engine.log counts every malformed call. It would have said 8, not 4, on 2026-09-22. A cut-off named call reaches the client once, not twice. Disconnects appear as `finish: abort` with no `ERROR … BUG`, so the routing statistics and the #91 instruments stop counting robin's window closes as length cuts.
